hfgt_toolbox.HFGTToolbox.GISDirectory2SysMLDictAuto(inputDirectoryPath, maxRows=None, maxFilesPerDirectory=None)

Given a directory as input, process all GIS-type files into a SysML- compliant Dictionary via the relevant function. The GIS files in the directory must be either .csv or .shp files to be processed. Any non .csv or .shp files will be skipped.

For each GIS file, if it is accompanied by a .yml file, whose filename is exactly the same as the file to which it refers (e.g. “data1.csv” is sitting alongside a .yml file called “data1.csv.yml”), it will be processed according to the instructions in that .yml file. If present, the .yml file must contain two keys:

  • class_name: The name of the class, e.g. “PowerPlant”.

  • idx_column_name: The name of the column that uniquely identifies each row, e.g. “name”.

It can also contain:

  • max_rows: The maximum number of rows to process. If this key is not present, the value from maxRows (the argument to this function) will be used instead.

If a GIS file is not accompanied by a .yml file, it will be processed as if its class_name is “Object”, and each object will be assigned an increasing id (“Object1”, “Object2”, etc). In this way, the .yml files are not required - they just improve the model.

Parameters:

  • inputDirectoryPath (str) – The path of the input directory.

  • maxRows (int, Optional) – The maximum number of rows to process for each dataset. If max_rows is present in a dataset’s corresponding .yml file, this value will be overridden.

  • maxFilesPerDirectory (int, Optional) – The maximum number of files to process in each directory. (useful when there may be directories containing 1000s of CSV files that you don’t need to include in the model.

Returns:

The LFES package representing the SysML model.

Return type:

dict

packSetSystemProcess()

This function computes the set of all possible REFINED transportation processes in the system. This set of processes includes storage at a certain buffer element and transportation from one buffer element to all other buffer elements present in the system.

populateInputData()

This function populates this LFES’s attributes with data loaded from either an XML or SysML file. The data is loaded from this LFES’s inputFilePath, validated, and then used to populate the myKeys attribute.

After the data is loaded, the standardizeInputFilePath() function is called. This builds a standardized filename, based on several of this LFES’ attributes e.g. scenario, runCode, etc. During this step, if the inputFilePath does not follow this standard naming convention, the input file is copied into an Archive/ folder and the input file is renamed to the standardized name. inputFilePath is then adjusted to this standardised name.

Several globals are set during the execution of this function, based on the corresponding entries in the input data file:

  • analysisMethod

  • inputDataFormat

These are stored as globals in order to avoid needing to pass them around to many other functions.

The logging level is set to DEBUG from here onwards if verboseMode = True.

Raises:

ValueError – If any errors arise, for example an unexpected file type, LFES name containing whitespace characters, etc. A ValueError is also raised if the input data does not contain any operands.

hfgt_toolbox.HFGTToolbox.df2SysMLDict(df, myClass=None, idxColumnName=None)

Given a Pandas DataFrame, and the name that should be assigned to each instance (e.g. “Substation”, “Power Plant”, etc), and the name of the column that uniquely identifies each row, convert the DataFrame into a SysML-compliant dictionary.

Note: Originally idxColumnName was ‘idxColumn’ (the index of the column which is the identifier), but I (MS) changed this to idxColumnName as I felt it made more sense and was easier to use (no need to figure out the index of the id column, and no issue if the id column is a different column index when calling this function across multiple files such as via GISDirectory2SysMLFile).

Parameters:

  • df (pd.DataFrame) – The input Pandas DataFrame.

  • myClass (str) – The name that should be assigned to each instance. If None, each instance will have the class “Object”.

  • idxColumnName (str) – The name of the column that uniquely identifies each row, which will appear as the name of each item in the SysML dictionary. If None, the id will be generated as Object1, Object2 and so on.

Returns:

A SysML-compliant dictionary representing the DataFrame.

Return type:

dict

hfgt_toolbox.HFGTToolbox.importInputData(inputFilePath)

The function creates an LFES instance and populates it by reading the data stored within the specified inputFilePath. The LFES instance is returned.

Note that the inputFilePath must be either an XML or a SysML file, i.e. its suffix must be either ‘.xml’ or ‘.sysml’. If it is not, populateInputData will raise an error.

The constructor of the LFES class instantiates many of its attributes. Several attributes are then initialised by both populateInputData and by this function. This function specifically sets the following attributes:

  • inputFilePath is set to the inputFilePath argument passed to this function.

  • outputFileName is automatically set based on the name of the LFES, the inputDataFormat, scenario, and runCode (which is a YYYY-MM-DD string based on the git commit date).

  • outputFilePath is by joining LFES’s outputDirectory with outputFileName above. Note that the directory is hardcoded, and is initialised by the constructor of the LFES class.

  • juliaOutputFilePath is overwritten so that it is joined with outputFileName above. Prior to being overwritten by this function, juliaOutputFilePath is a hardcoded directory path (similarly set by the LFES class’ constructor).

Parameters:

inputFilePath (pl.Path) – The file path to import data from.

Raises:

FileNotFoundError – If the specified inputFilePath does not exist.

Returns:

An LFES data structure with completed analytical calculations.

Return type:

LFES
